clue.text: Take in a smile as it develops

indicators.note: as something develops it changes shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone absorbs a smile as it slowly spreads across a face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' signals the anagram of A SMILE AS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in knowledge or food is to absorb it fully, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Container needed by group outside a church?

indicators.note: the word for group sits outside the other pieces, wrapping round them

parts.note: a set is a group of things belonging together

explanation.surface: A container is wanted by a crowd gathered outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed packet holding sugar, shampoo or herbs is a kind of container.

clue.text: Unenlightened Italian bloke losing head with worker

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: signor is the Italian title for a man, so an Italian bloke
a worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A clueless Italian man is beheaded while working alongside a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the S from SIGNOR, leaving IGNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unenlightened lacks knowledge, which is what being uninformed or uneducated means.

clue.text: Flatmate may be more alert, ignoring parking

indicators.note: ignoring a thing means leaving it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: sharper means keener, more alert
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A flatmate might be more watchful, except about where to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring parking' takes the P out of SHARPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate splits a flat's rent and space with you, so is one who shares.

clue.text: Struggles, seeing Greek tech company succeeded

parts.note: Apple is a well-known technology company
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone struggles on finding that a Greek technology firm came out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to wrestle or struggle, so the plural verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Animal's temperature in helium perhaps going up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
the temperature letter goes inside the word for helium perhaps

parts.note: helium is an example of a gas

explanation.surface: An animal's body temperature rises in a balloon of helium.
explanation.walkthrough: T inside GAS gives GATS; 'going up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal, so the specific creature fits the general word.

clue.text: Horse's insect problem making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting insect
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A horse's trouble with flies is returning.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild horse of the American West is a breed of horse.

clue.text: Car stops outside north of Rugby for service given

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British car

indicators.note: the word for stops goes outside the picked letter, enclosing it

parts.note: stations are stopping places on a railway line

indicators.note: in a down clue the north of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A car halts beyond the northern end of Rugby to give some service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of' works because this is a down clue, where the top letter comes first. Rugby is a town in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministrations are acts of help or care given to someone, i.e. services rendered.

clue.text: Sort of vehicle difficult to pass initially

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Some kind of vehicle proves tricky to overtake at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a fixed rigid roof is called by this name, a type of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Pressure confuses crew on Queen Elizabeth and another vessel

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
to addle is to muddle or confuse
a team is a crew working together
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Pressure throws the crew aboard the liner Queen Elizabeth, and another ship is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Elizabeth is a famous liner, hence 'another vessel'; here it only gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle-driven steamship is a vessel, distinct from the liner named in the clue.

clue.text: Live close to region developed with hub

indicators.note: land that is developed is built over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Living near a district that has been built up around a central hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' signals the anagram of REGION and HUB.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to neighbour something is to be next to or adjoin it.

clue.text: Called boy attending bride perhaps starting to doubt

parts.note: a page boy attends a bride at a wedding

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A page boy at a wedding was summoned, beginning to have misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them by name over a speaker, so called.

clue.text: Women enveloped by strain may be able to move fast

indicators.note: the women letter is wrapped inside the word for strain

parts.note: to sift is to strain or sieve

explanation.surface: Women gripped by tension might nonetheless move quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift is an adjective meaning quick or rapid in motion.

clue.text: Spring pudding as butt of joke?

parts.note: April is a spring month
a fool is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream

explanation.surface: A seasonal dessert becomes the target of a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a creamy British fruit dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked by a prank on the first of April is the target of the joke.

clue.text: Provoked editor after incident

indicators.note: the editor abbreviation comes after the incident word

parts.note: an occasion is an event or incident

explanation.surface: An editor was stirred to anger following some event.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion something is to cause or bring it about, so provoked is a synonym.

clue.text: Boxer during break must be a practical type

indicators.note: the boxer comes during the break, so inside that word

parts.note: a rest is a break
Muhammad Ali is the crossword's favourite boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer resting between rounds must take a pragmatic view.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sees things as they are and acts sensibly is a practical sort.

clue.text: Independent people welcoming clubs' lack of movement

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the clubs letter goes inside

parts.note: a nation is a people
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Independent folk who welcome clubs show little sign of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing at all is a lack of action or movement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cuts speech oddly in pieces

indicators.note: the odd letters go in the word for pieces

parts.note: bits are pieces

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone chops a speech up strangely into fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks S, E, C from speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two parts, so the verb is a specific kind of cut.

clue.text: Try very hard except being occupied by 6 and university

indicators.note: being occupied by means other letters sit inside it

parts.note: but means except
refers to the answer to 6 down, the animal

explanation.surface: Make an all-out effort, except when a deer and a university move in.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to strain oneself making a huge effort.

clue.text: Sign accepting he's an authority on words

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for sign holds the other piece

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
he's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An astrological sign welcomes him as an expert in vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is an authoritative reference on words.

clue.text: Slight case of reserve in front of enthusiast

indicators.note: the first piece comes in front of the second
a case is the outside of something, so the outer letters are taken

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, as in a film buff

explanation.surface: A minor brush-off: the edge of a reserve player standing before a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub, and a rebuff is a curt refusal or snub.

clue.text: Children may be a bone of contention

definitions.meaning: a disputed point or matter under debate

explanation.surface: Children can be the cause of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both offspring and a point in dispute.

clue.text: Charge defined by Latin dictionaries

indicators.note: the answer is set within the bounds of these words, lying across them

explanation.surface: An accusation whose meaning is laid down in Latin reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to formally charge someone with a crime.

clue.text: Stung by soldiers finding range

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
bit is past tense of bite, as an insect stings

explanation.surface: Soldiers find themselves stung while finding the range.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a sphere of influence or scope, so a range.

clue.text: Sacks reserves

definitions.meaning: claims or reserves something, as in bagging a seat

explanation.surface: Sacks held in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sacks and to claim or reserve something.

clue.text: Area of company making sweeper cover busy road

indicators.note: the sweeper word covers, so goes around, the other letters

parts.note: a broom is a sweeper

indicators.note: busy means bustling, stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company's patch has a street sweeper covering a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is the anagram signal, and 'cover' makes the sweeper word go around the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where a company's directors meet is an area of the firm.

clue.text: Not working after notice, and stop claiming benefit

indicators.note: the not-working word comes after the notice word

parts.note: a sign is a notice
off means not working, as a machine is off

explanation.surface: Not working after being given notice, so stop collecting the dole.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'signing on' means registering for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for ending a claim for unemployment benefit, opposite of signing on.

clue.text: Relation with a right to be less than explicit

parts.note: an uncle is a relation

explanation.surface: A relative who has a right to be vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not clear or plain is less than explicit, a near synonym.
